notes_list.title: Friedel–Crafts Comparison
notes_list.basic_overview: Both are electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions catalysed by Lewis acids, but one installs an alkyl group and the other an acyl group.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Alkylation: alkyl electrophile, possible rearrangement and polyalkylation. Acylation: acylium ion, generally no carbocation rearrangement and usually monoacylation because the ring becomes deactivated by the acyl group.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Both are electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions catalysed by Lewis acids, but one installs an alkyl group and the other an acyl group. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
